clue.text: Poor Joe B getting totally disheartened? Admiration often expressed for his opponent

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters that follow are taken apart and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: totally disheartened says the whole inside of the word getting is removed, leaving just its two outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Joe Biden, faring badly and losing all spirit, while his rival keeps praising himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totally disheartened' strips ETTIN from GETTING, leaving GG; 'Poor' then rearranges JOE, B, GG and ADMIRATION into the four-word phrase. His opponent was Donald Trump, fond of boasting about his own performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump repeatedly boasted of his own record with this exact self-congratulating phrase, so it is the line his opponent was often heard to say.

clue.text: Is to talk to police after money's disappeared

indicators.note: after places the words is and to talk to police behind the money letter

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing on accomplices to the police

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to go to the police once cash has vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has disappeared is lost or absent, not where it should be.

clue.text: Wealthy American's brother keeping silent in turn

indicators.note: in turn asks for the name to be turned round and read from its end

parts.note: Harpo was the Marx Brother who never spoke on screen

explanation.surface: A rich American's sibling stays quiet when it is his turn to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Oprah Winfrey, the talk-show host, is one of the richest self-made women in the United States.

clue.text: Punch American — listen to riot outside

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for American
to riot is to run wild, so the letters of listen go into disorder

explanation.surface: An American throws a punch and tells the listener the crowd is about to riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to riot' turns LISTEN into NILSET, and 'outside' wraps that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail set is a carpenter's punch, a small steel tool used to drive nail heads below the surface.

clue.text: Intelligence but not at the top?

definitions.meaning: the inside information or facts on a matter
placed near the bottom, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Getting the full inside story is slang for intelligence, and anything set near the floor sits far from the top.

clue.text: Looking intelligent, like a Member of Parliament?

definitions.meaning: having a wise, bespectacled air, like a scholar
a group of owls is called a parliament, so a member of one is that bird

explanation.surface: Someone resembling a politician puts on a clever expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are the traditional emblem of wisdom, and a gathering of owls is known as a parliament.

clue.text: Having division speak badly of West Ham?

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for disrespecting them
West Ham United is a London football club, often just called United

explanation.surface: A fan criticises West Ham, perhaps for their place in the football division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division' looks like a football league table, but it means split or disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A group that is split by quarrels and factions has division within it.

clue.text: Inspirational leader isn't now failing …

indicators.note: failing means falling apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A once-great leader is no longer in decline, or so it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of ISNTNOW, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill led Britain through the Second World War and is remembered for his rousing speeches.

clue.text: … in short, that is correct — I'm as dynamic as the very best governments?

indicators.note: dynamic suggests movement and change, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: i.e. is the short Latin form of that is
taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone boasts of being as energetic as the finest regimes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue. 'dynamic' rearranges IE, CORRECT, IM and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems where power goes to people chosen for ability are, in theory, government by the most able.

clue.text: Government policy co-ordinator that's arguably not all there

indicators.note: not all there says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A government official who oversees a policy is, some say, mentally lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers call an official appointed to oversee a policy area, such as a drugs or energy chief, by this Russian imperial title.

clue.text: Taking unrealistic view of claims by agent and Adele?

parts.note: a dealer or agent would say of himself that he deals
Adele is a famous singer, who could say of herself that she sings

explanation.surface: Someone sees an agent and a pop star through rose-tinted glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims by' covers both people: the agent says I DEAL, and Adele says I SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone as perfect, rather than as they really are, is viewing them in an unrealistic light.

clue.text: Scares female away, which one's entitled to

indicators.note: away says the letter for female is sent off, taken out of the word for scares

parts.note: frights are scares or shocks

explanation.surface: Something frightens a woman off, and this is what she is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Entitlements, such as legal or human ones, are things a person may justly claim.

clue.text: Elected idiot state's accommodated — there's no sense in it

parts.note: a candidate voted into office is said to be in

indicators.note: accommodated means given room, so the word for state holds the idiot inside it

parts.note: to state is to say
a nit is a fool, a nitwit

explanation.surface: An elected fool has been housed by the state, which seems quite senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is the complete absence of good sense or reason.

clue.text: See 1
School agree head's showing great enthusiasm

indicators.note: to school is to train or drill, so the letters of agree are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A school's governors agree their head teacher is showing real zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun but is the verb that rearranges AGREE into EAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness or impatient desire is a strong enthusiasm for something.

clue.text: Pained by return of crazy government?

indicators.note: return of means the letters are turned back to front

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt by the comeback of a mad administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hurt, whether by a bee or a cutting remark, is to be pained.

clue.text: The last time doctor's coming round

indicators.note: coming round says the combined letters turn about and read backwards

parts.note: an age is a period of time
MO stands for medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: At the final moment, a doctor finally arrives to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end of anything.

clue.text: What gives couple authority?

parts.note: a couple is made of a man and his date, and the whole is an official authority to act

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a question about a pair, but split the answer into a fellow and his partner for the evening to see the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters give a government official authority to carry out its policies; that authority is what the word means.

clue.text: Soldier's new bride touring capital

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the jumbled letters go around the capital
new means made afresh, so the letters of bride are rearranged

parts.note: Riga is the capital city of Latvia

explanation.surface: A soldier's newly wed wife goes on a trip around a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like a wedding detail but rearranges the bride's letters, which then go round the Latvian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer ranking above a colonel and commanding a brigade is a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Boyish young ladies wearing sports skirts

indicators.note: skirts as a verb means goes around the edge of, so sports encloses the next word

parts.note: games are sports
if you are in a dress you are wearing it

explanation.surface: Tomboyish girls are dressed in sports skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like the garment but is the verb meaning surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim girl with mischievous, boyish charm.

clue.text: Huge rear — about to slip into underwear, the biggest of its kind

indicators.note: rear means the back end, so only the final letter of huge is taken
to slip into means the short word for about is slid inside the word for underwear

parts.note: in British English a vest is an undershirt
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A large backside is about to squeeze into a pair of undies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Huge rear' is not a bottom: rear means the last letter of Huge. A vest in Britain is an undergarment, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain on Earth, its name is used for the greatest example of anything.

clue.text: Carol uplifted by one's spiritual awareness?

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a carol is a song
one is I, and one's means one is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A Christmas carol lifts someone's spirits into a mystic insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is mystical knowledge of spiritual truths, as the Gnostics claimed.

clue.text: Where you learn fellow in charge intended to be taken seriously

parts.note: uni is short for university, a place of learning
Ron is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A university fellow in charge of something insists he means it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' suggests an academic post, but it is simply a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant without irony is meant sincerely and literally.

clue.text: Married before the end of three months — she's in the club

parts.note: September, November and December all end in these five letters

explanation.surface: A woman married just before the year's end, and is now pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the club' is British slang for pregnant, which fits married neatly; here it means belonging to a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who belongs to a club is one of its signed-up associates.

clue.text: Man's timeless lesson

indicators.note: timeless read as time-less means the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: a mortal is a man, a human being

explanation.surface: Humanity's eternal lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The point a fable teaches is the lesson to be drawn from it.

clue.text: Could be Chinese food mainly at the back

parts.note: fare is food, as in a menu's fare
main means the sea, so at the back at sea is the nautical astern

explanation.surface: Chinese food mostly comes towards the end of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' looks like 'mostly' but means 'on the main', at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the East Asian region, so Chinese is one example of this description.

clue.text: Lamented ignorant broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out over the air, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: rude can mean ignorant or uneducated, as in a rude peasant

explanation.surface: Someone mourns an ill-informed programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To have regretted something deeply is to have lamented it.

clue.text: Carry On Priests? Unlikely

indicators.note: unlikely says the word priests is reshaped into an improbable form

explanation.surface: A title for an imagined Carry On comedy film about clergy, dismissed as improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were a long-running series of British slapstick comedies, such as Carry On Nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going in spite of difficulty is to carry on.

clue.text: Quarantine on island long overdue

parts.note: so late means very much overdue

explanation.surface: A quarantine on an island has been put off for far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine someone is to keep them apart from others.
